hints: Look closely at the carbonyl group in each structure and decide whether each compound is an aldehyde or a ketone.
Notice that compound T has a $\text{CH}_3\text{C=O}$ group while compound U has a $\text{H-C=O}$ group, so think about which classic test needs a methyl ketone.
Recall what happens with alkaline aqueous iodine and link the yellow precipitate of $\text{CHI}_3$ to only one of these two structures.
walkthrough:
**Identify T and U from their structures**

First, read the displayed formulae carefully. T is $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, which is pentan-2-one, a ketone.

U is $\text{HCOCH(CH}_3\text{)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, which is 2-methylbutanal, an aldehyde.

$$\text{T = pentan-2-one, U = 2-methylbutanal}$$

**Apply the iodoform test rule**

The tri-iodomethane (iodoform) test with alkaline aqueous iodine gives a yellow precipitate only with methyl ketones ($\text{CH}_3\text{CO-R}$) and ethanal.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{COR} + 3\text{I}_2 + 4\text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{CHI}_3 + \text{RCOO}^- + 3\text{I}^- + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Conclude the correct distinction**

T has the $\text{CH}_3\text{CO-}$ group, so it gives a positive result with yellow $\text{CHI}_3$. U is an aldehyde with no $\text{CH}_3\text{CO-}$ group, so it stays negative.

That difference means alkaline aqueous iodine cleanly distinguishes T from U.

options.A: Incorrect. Both have formula $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$ but T is a ketone and U is an aldehyde, so they are functional group (structural) isomers, not stereoisomers. Stereoisomers need the same connectivity with different spatial arrangement.
options.B: Correct. T is a methyl ketone and gives a positive iodoform test (yellow precipitate of $\text{CHI}_3$ with decolourisation of iodine) while U does not. This is a classic distinguishing test.
options.C: Incorrect. Both $\text{LiAlH}_4$ and $\text{NaBH}_4$ reduce aldehydes and ketones to alcohols. T (pentan-2-one) would be reduced to pentan-2-ol by either reagent.
options.D: Incorrect. Oxidation of the primary alcohol 3-methylbutan-1-ol, $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, gives 3-methylbutanal, $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHCH}_2\text{CHO}$. U is 2-methylbutanal, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(CH}_3\text{)CHO}$, which would come from 2-methylbutan-1-ol.
